BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.

- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).

- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update & Disclosure Letter

**Preliminary note on the Seller's preamble.** The statements that the positions are "market standard", "settled at principal level", "agreed" and "FINAL" are counterparty assertions only. Under playbook 0.4/6.3 they carry no weight until confirmed through our own authority process. We have no record of principal-level agreement from Amelia Frost on any of these items. Treat every "FINAL" marking as the Seller's opening position.

---

**SPA-N-001 – General liability cap (cl 12.1)**
- Seller: 20% / AUD 4,800,000.
- Buyer wants: 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- **Recommendation: REJECT; counter at 25% / AUD 6.0m.** The 20% figure coincides with our fallback, but the fallback is usable only with prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this draft – none exists, and a matching number does not clear it.

**SPA-N-002 – De minimis & basket (cl 12.2)**
- Seller: de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only recovery.
- Buyer wants: de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; first-dollar recovery once exceeded.
- **Recommendation: REJECT; counter with playbook figures and tipping (first-dollar) basket.** The Seller's thresholds are 5x our position and the excess-only mechanic alone could strand up to AUD 250k of valid loss.

**SPA-N-003 – General claims time limit (cl 12.3/13)**
- Seller: 18 months; plus a default rule that any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly excluded.
- Buyer wants: 24 months; limitations apply only to the categories they expressly name.
- **Recommendation: REJECT both limbs; counter at 24 months and delete the "applies to all Claims" default.** 18 months is an unauthorised fallback (no Amelia Frost approval) and the default rule is a hidden general-regime override contrary to playbook category separation.

**SPA-N-004 – Fundamental/Title regime**
- Seller: capacity and title warranties subject to general caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity".
- Buyer wants: separate regime – 100% of price cap, minimum six years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation: REJECT outright; insert a standalone Fundamental Warranty regime.** Capping title at 20% means we could pay AUD 24m and recover AUD 4.8m if we do not own the shares – "administrative simplicity" is not a reason.

**SPA-N-005 – Fraud carve-out (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5)**
- Seller: limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" – no fraud carve-out.
- Buyer wants: fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- **Recommendation: REJECT; non-negotiable insertion of a full fraud/wilful-misconduct carve-out.** This is a no-waiver item under the playbook and the Seller's drafting would purport to limit liability for its own fraud.

**SPA-N-006 – Disclosure scope (Sch 7 / DL 1.1–1.2)**
- Seller: general disclosure of the whole data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and public records.
- Buyer wants: specific, fair disclosure only; no whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Recommendation: REJECT DL 1.1–1.2 and the Sch 7 general-disclosure mechanic; accept only specific disclosures that fairly identify the matter and its implications.** Whole-room disclosure converts every warranty into a diligence exercise and is the single biggest value leak in this package.

**SPA-N-007 – Buyer knowledge qualifier (cl 8.3)**
- Seller: no claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew of, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records.
- Buyer wants: delete the blanket exclusion; any qualifier limited to named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry; never applies to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation: DELETE cl 8.3 in full.** "Discoverable" imputes constructive knowledge of the entire data room and public registers, which combined with SPA-N-006 would hollow out the warranty package entirely.

**SPA-N-008 – Bluefen consent (cl 3/6.3)**
- Seller: reasonable endeavours; condition satisfied on delivery of a written consent. DL para 2 confirms no final consent and no evidence of cl 11.3 conditions being met.
- Buyer wants: a Completion condition requiring an effective consent **and** evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied before Completion.
- **Recommendation: REJECT; redraft as a hard condition precedent (effective consent + condition evidence), not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours is insufficient.** Bluefen is ~30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6m) and the Seller's own letter admits the consent is still outstanding.

**SPA-N-009 – Riverlark facility (cl 2/7)**
- Seller: ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release to be provided after Completion. DL para 3 confirms not repaid, no discharge.
- Buyer wants: current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases delivered at Completion.
- **Recommendation: REJECT post-completion release; require payout letter, direct pay-down in the funds flow and executed releases/PPSR discharges at Completion.** Any post-completion mechanic needs an irrevocable bank undertaking plus Amelia Frost approval – neither is on the table.

**SPA-N-010 – Employee bonuses (DD-005 / funds flow)**
- Seller: AUD 420,000 bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised. DL para 5 confirms omission and is silent on on-costs.
- Buyer wants: AUD 420,000 plus triggered payroll tax, super and other on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item or an express Seller-funded obligation.
- **Recommendation: REJECT silent exclusion; insert a dedicated line item (bonuses + on-costs) or Seller-funding covenant and confirm treatment under the debt-free/cash-free mechanics.** As drafted, the Buyer inherits the liability after Completion with no price adjustment.

**SPA-N-011 – Ironquay IP indemnity (cl 11.1)**
- Seller: indemnity confined to the SOW3 payment; considered adequate. DL para 4: cl 7.3 makes transfer of SOW3 Project Materials conditional on cleared payment; DD-010 shows AUD 180k open but is not bank-verified; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the room.
- Buyer wants: broader indemnity covering title to and use of the SOW3 Project Materials and any Ironquay claim, while preserving the cure (pay and obtain assignment).
- **Recommendation: COUNTER with a broadened indemnity (loss from non-ownership, third-party claims, re-procurement) and a Completion deliverable of either a paid receipt + confirmatory assignment or a Seller-funded cure.** The AUD 180k is unverified in either direction, so the indemnity must cover the IP outcome, not just one invoice.

**SPA-N-012 – Export/privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6 / DD-006)**
- Seller: "preliminary operational matter", not expected to be material. DL para 6: ~1,240 records sent to an unintended external address; access, scope and notification duty unknown; investigation preliminary; no breach admitted.
- Buyer wants: log preservation, a completed investigation, ongoing updates, and a specific indemnity/covenant structure that does not prejudge the outcome.
- **Recommendation: Do NOT accept the "not material" characterisation, but do NOT assert a confirmed breach or numeric demand either; require a preservation/investigation covenant, pre-Completion update, and a specific indemnity for notification and regulatory costs if triggered.** The facts are open in both directions and the Buyer should lock in process and allocation rather than a conclusion.

**SPA-N-013 – Sandbar renewals (DD-008/DD-011, AUD 330,000)**
- Seller: ordinary-course operating costs. DL para 8: three renewals of AUD 110k each; unclear whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- Buyer wants: an assessment of timing, scope and termination rights before any classification.
- **Recommendation: HOLD – no automatic Debt classification or price deduction; request renewal terms, termination rights and accrual status, then decide between working-capital treatment, specific indemnity or nothing.** The Seller's label is unsupported, but so would be a reflexive deduction.

**SPA-N-014 – Category separation**
- Seller: single general regime applying to Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant claims; "all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise".
- Buyer wants: Title/Fundamental, Tax, IP, payment obligations and covenants each on their own limitation terms with no default sweep-up.
- **Recommendation: REJECT; redraft cl 12/13 so each category has express terms and the general cap/basket/time limit applies only to General Warranty Claims.** The Seller's default clause operates as a hidden override of every category we have negotiated separately.

**SPA-N-015 – Title verification (DD-012)**
- Seller: title to 100% evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012. DL para 10 admits this is the source relied on, not independent verification.
- Buyer wants: independent evidence of ownership, absence of encumbrances (including PPSR and Riverlark security) and Seller authority; share transfer and board approvals as Completion deliverables.
- **Recommendation: DO NOT accept DD-012 as sufficient; obtain ASIC extract, PPSR search, constitution, officer's certificate and share certificate/transfer, and keep the title warranty on the fundamental regime (SPA-N-004).** An internal register supplied by the Seller is a starting point, not proof.

**SPA-N-016 – Tax/IP open terms**
- Seller: tax and IP warranties "settled" under the general regime (20% cap, 18 months, AUD 250k basket).
- Buyer wants: Tax and IP remain OPEN and are negotiated as separate categories; no unlimited liability assumed, no resolution assumed.
- **Recommendation: REJECT the "settled" characterisation; record Tax and IP as open with placeholders for a separate tax indemnity/covenant and IP warranty regime.** Nothing has been agreed through our authority process, and folding them into the general regime would be the SPA-N-014 override by another name.

---

**Summary for the deal team.** Of the 16 items, none can be accepted as drafted. Two (SPA-N-001 cap and SPA-N-003 time limit) sit at our conditional fallback numbers but require Amelia Frost's written authority identifying this draft before we could move – recommend we do **not** seek that authority yet, as conceding both without reciprocal movement on thresholds, disclosure and knowledge would be a poor trade. The highest-priority blockers are SPA-N-004/005/014 (regime structure), SPA-N-006/007 (disclosure and knowledge), and SPA-N-008/009 (Bluefen and Riverlark Completion mechanics). Suggest the mark-up leads with those and presents the cap/basket/time points as a package.
